do_not_assume: Stop when the slow component or infrastructure constraint is identified with repeatable evidence; do not prescribe a web farm solely from the symptom.
start_with: Confirm the Rock version. In v19, capture the Page Load Time diagnostic trace for the affected page.
Identify whether one block or component dominates the trace.
Reproduce at a known time and record whether the issue is constant, intermittent, or load-dependent.
Inspect IIS application-pool startup, idle timeout, preload, recycling, and dynamic-compression settings.
Determine whether the page invokes Data Views, Reports, analytics, plugins, APIs, or long-running database operations.
Inspect whether snapshot isolation is enabled and whether supported read workloads are eligible for `RockContextReadOnly` or `RockContextAnalytics`. Install Rock
Compare the symptom with CPU, database, network, and provider telemetry.
Stop when the slow component or infrastructure constraint is identified with repeatable evidence; do not prescribe a web farm solely from the symptom.
branches.title: A Rock page is slow

start_with: Confirm that requests are reaching more than one web node.
Identify the Rock File Type or upload path used by the missing asset.
If the File Type uses node-local File System storage, move the design toward cloud-backed or database-backed storage.
If the file was uploaded directly to a node-local content directory, verify whether that directory is synchronized across nodes.
Request the same asset through each node or controlled gateway routing.
Stop when every node can serve the same asset and the storage or synchronization owner is documented.
branches.title: Files or images work intermittently in a web farm
branches.when: Files or images work intermittently in a web farm

start_with: Confirm that the environment uses multiple web nodes.
Inspect the gateway’s session-affinity configuration.
Trace a representative check-in client across consecutive requests.
Confirm that the client remains on the same node for the session.
Stop when the session remains stable through an end-to-end check-in journey.
branches.title: Check-in loses state or behaves differently between requests
branches.when: Check-in loses state or behaves differently between requests

do_not_assume: Do not use v20.0 alpha shared-locking release notes as evidence that a v19 farm is safe.
start_with: Confirm the exact Rock version.
For Rock 19.0, inspect every node’s web configuration and identify which node is allowed to run jobs.
Ensure only one node is configured as the job runner.
Review job history and downstream effects for duplicate execution.
Do not use v20.0 alpha shared-locking release notes as evidence that a v19 farm is safe.
Stop when a single v19 job-running node is proven and a subsequent scheduled execution produces only the expected run. Configure a Rock Web Farm
branches.title: A scheduled job runs more than once in a web farm
branches.when: A scheduled job runs more than once in a web farm

start_with: Confirm that the Spark web-farm license is active.
Confirm that exactly one supported message-bus transport is active.
Verify that the gateway, database, and expected web nodes are running.
Confirm that Rock is installed on each node.
Restart all nodes after web-farm activation or configuration changes.
Inspect the Web Farm page and web-farm log for startup, shutdown, status, or leadership events.
Confirm that every expected node appears.
Stop when node membership and message-bus communication are stable.
branches.title: A web-farm node is missing or appears unresponsive
branches.when: A web-farm node is missing or appears unresponsive

start_with: Confirm that the environment is a Rock 19.0 web farm.
Verify that the route itself was saved correctly.
Restart each node so the route table is refreshed before the normal application-pool cycle.
Test the route against every node or through repeated controlled gateway requests.
Stop when all nodes resolve the route consistently.
branches.title: A new page route works on only some nodes
branches.when: A new page route works on only some nodes

start_with: Identify the database type: Azure SQL Database, SQL Server on an Azure VM, or local/self-hosted SQL Server.
Verify the server name, database name, Rock-specific login, and connection target without exposing the password.
For Azure SQL Database, verify the login and `master` user, the `dbmanager` and `loginmanager` roles, and the database user’s `db_owner` membership.
For a self-hosted two-server deployment, verify TCP 1433 is permitted from the Rock web server’s address.
Confirm that SQL Server is private rather than generally internet-exposed.
Test the Rock-specific SQL login independently.
Stop when the Rock web server can connect using the intended restricted identity and network path. Configure SQL Server
branches.title: Rock cannot connect to SQL Server
branches.when: Rock cannot connect to SQL Server

start_with: Confirm that the requested feature is part of the documented Rock web-server prerequisites.
Obtain installation media matching the Windows Server version.
Mount the media.
Set the alternate feature source to its `sources\sxs` directory.
Retry installation.
Stop when IIS, the applicable ASP.NET 4.x role service, WebSocket Protocol, Application Initialization, and .NET Framework 3.5 Features are present.
branches.title: Windows cannot install a required server feature
branches.when: Windows cannot install a required server feature

start_with: Confirm that `RockContextReadOnly` is present and points to the intended database.
Test basic connectivity and data availability.
Identify whether the Data View contains a plugin or filter that performs writes.
If writes are required, enable **Disable Use Of Read Only Context** for that specific Data View.
Retest the operation against the primary context.
Stop when the operation succeeds and its context selection is documented.
branches.title: A Data View or report fails against the read-only database
branches.when: A Data View or report fails against the read-only database

start_with: Confirm the installation is Rock 19.0 or another version documented to support the setting.
Verify that the connection-string name is exactly `RockContextAnalytics`.
Confirm that it points to the intended read-only target.
Test Giving Analytics, Attendance Analytics, and Pledge Analytics separately.
Observe the target database or connection telemetry during the test.
Stop when the intended analytics traffic is observed on the target context.
branches.title: Analytics still load the primary database
branches.when: Analytics still load the primary database

start_with: Confirm a valid certificate is installed and bound to the intended IIS site.
Inspect the Rock Site record for **Require Encryption**.
Enable the setting for the internal and external Rock sites where applicable.
Test direct HTTP and HTTPS requests from outside the server.
In a farm, confirm certificate coverage and binding behavior across the gateway and nodes.
Stop when HTTP consistently reaches the intended HTTPS endpoint and the presented certificate is valid. Intro to Internal Hosting
branches.title: HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS
branches.when: HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS

entrypoint: Choose the branch whose symptom matches the user's task, then inspect the live records before making changes.
